findings.title: Cleanup deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1, including already-scheduled and non-SMS ones
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: SMS`, no `scheduled: false`, and no date filter. It matches any WorkflowReminder with retryCount >= 2. retryCount is only incremented on failure, but a row that failed twice and later succeeded keeps its count, and the success path (lines ~169-177) sets `scheduled: true` and `referenceId` without resetting it. Such a row is still deleted by this cron. The Twilio message stays queued, but the DB row holding `referenceId` is gone, so a later booking cancellation or reschedule can no longer cancel the SMS. Email reminders are also swept up. Fix: scope the retry clause to `method: SMS, scheduled: false`, and/or reset retryCount on success.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole cron loop
findings.body: The catch block now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update` without its own try/catch. If that update throws (e.g. the row was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation, which makes Prisma throw P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are skipped for this run, and the handler returns an error. One bad row can therefore block every other reminder. Wrap the increment in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany` with a `where` that tolerates missing rows.

findings.title: retryCount incremented from a stale in-memory value instead of atomically
findings.body: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` uses the value read at the start of the run. If two cron invocations overlap (the scheduler is not guarded by a lock here), both read the same count and both write count+1, so failures are under-counted and the reminder can be retried more times than the intended limit. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` avoids this.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry/deletion behaviour
findings.body: The PR changes what gets scheduled, retried and deleted (threshold `gt: 1`, increment on both failure paths, new cleanup clause), but adds no tests for the retry count sequence, the deletion threshold, or the interaction with already-scheduled reminders. The bug above would have been caught by a test of a reminder that fails once and then succeeds.
